prompt_en: An atmospheric environmental photograph of visible electrical phenomena aboard a small survey ship crossing a storm-black estuary in the last blue minute before a squall engulfs the shoreline. The electrical effects unfold in the same shutter moment. Portray the woman from the supplied appearance reference, using the image as a face-and-hairstyle appearance reference. Preserve her soft oval face, dark almond-shaped eyes, straight slender nose, gently parted lips and small cheek beauty mark. Preserve her dark straight chin-length bob with fine loose center-fringe strands. Her particular face remains readable in three-quarter view, with a few damp strands catching warm cabin light. Inside the wheelhouse she is saving a weather log while shutting an inward-opening casement. Her worn olive rain shell hangs open over a slate knit turtleneck, its cuffs darkened by spray. Her left palm presses a curling log page flat against the fixed chart table; her right hand grips the nearby brass casement latch at shoulder height, elbow comfortably bent, pulling the pane toward its closed frame. The two forearms take separate visible paths to their targets. She leans slightly over the table, her shoulders angled toward the window, and turns her face enough for both eyes to remain visible as she notices the sharp electrical glow outside. Concentration parts her lips; the quiet warmth of her face makes the storm's scale feel close and personal. The lifted corner of the page, scattered droplets beside it and the narrowing window gap show what she is trying to protect. On the dry inboard end of the chart table, a compact oscilloscope gives the weather log a visible measurement source. Its single screen holds a captured signal as one continuous pale-green trace across a fine graticule, with readable V labels along the vertical voltage scale and ms labels along the horizontal time scale. A probe cable plugs into the front socket of this same oscilloscope; its small probe head rests beside the log, continuously connected back to that instrument. The screen occupies a small zone clear of her left hand, its faint green light touching only nearby dark varnish. Beyond the right-hand pane, the ship's short metal signal mast rises immediately outside the wheelhouse. Compact blue-violet corona brushes cling to two exposed sharp metal finials. Each delicate luminous thread emerges directly from a bare tip and fades within a few centimeters; dark air separates the two small brushes and surrounds the mast. Much farther away, a white branching lightning channel spreads horizontally inside the storm cloud, lighting a broad cloud volume from within. Its several forks are embedded high above the black sea horizon. The little near-field tip glows and the distant cloud-scale lightning have plainly different sizes, structures and physical origins. A rain curtain advances across the estuary behind the low shoreline. Across the window view, multiple near middle and far depth references are visible: crisp rain beads on the near frame, the mast on the foredeck and the low far shoreline. The bank recedes into rain-softened grey silhouettes so that far objects have lower contrast than near objects. Here the atmospheric effect agrees with weather and light: the squall's soft grey veil stays outside, lit by the cool flash. The near material detail remains as readable as requested, especially the sharp metal points, wet frame edges and both working hands. Use a horizontal 3:2 photographic frame. Frame a waist-up environmental portrait from inside the wheelhouse, the woman and her working hands in the left and lower foreground, the sharply pointed mast visible through the right pane, and the horizontal illuminated cloud occupying the upper background. Use a 35mm perspective with enough depth of field to read the metal tips, window mechanism, log and cloud branches together. A shaded amber chart lamp softly models her face and hands, the large lightning-lit cloud gives a brief cool reflection across wet glass, and the corona remains a small faint blue-violet source. Natural skin texture, rain beads and worn painted metal carry a restrained documentary color treatment and the tense intimacy of an observed working moment.
